articles.description: The handbag promoted as the "world's first T. rex leather product" didn't find a buyer at auction. Is it more chicken than dinosaur?

articles.description: US pastors, a Ugandan musician and salmon-friendly tech delivered good environmental news this week.

articles.description: A video of a knife attack sparked racist riots across the Northern Irish capital Belfast on Monday, with violence has now spreading across the United Kingdom. Keir Starmer says there will be "no tolerance" for rioters.

articles.title: Is there anything GLP-1 agonist drugs cannot do?
articles.description: Every other month, researchers find new uses for GLP-1 agonist drugs, like Mounjaro and Ozempic — now even as a treatment for substance abuse. It's classic drug repurposing, a technique that saved lives during COVID.

articles.title: UK: Defense Secretary John Healey quits in military spending dispute

articles.description: Beyond a headline-grabbing bronze, contemporary artworks draw attention to political power at an exhibition held at Bellevue Palace before the state building closes for renovation.

articles.title: Hungary makes major deal with Ukraine, a former enemy
articles.description: Hungarian Prime Minister Magyar has announced an agreement with Kyiv about rights for a Hungarian minority in Ukraine. It paves the way for Ukraine to start EU accession talks — unthinkable under Hungary's last leader.

articles.title: World Cup 2026: How an old song from Bosnia went viral
articles.description: Some have already called it the unofficial song of the 2026 World Cup. So how did a tune that was more than a decade old take the Balkans — and beyond — by storm?

articles.title: Neo-Nazi lost an east German election, but extremism remains
articles.description: A neo-Nazi candidate surprisingly lost a mayoral election by a small margin in the eastern state of Saxony. Many are relieved. But one win doesn't make the extremism problem go away.

articles.title: 'Disclosure Day': For Spielberg, aliens are not just fiction
articles.description: As Steven Spielberg releases a new film on extraterrestrials, here's a brief history of modern alien conspiracies and why scientists are now taking UFO reports seriously.

articles.title: World Cup: Edin Dzeko still strong for Bosnia-Herzegovina
articles.description: With so much unpleasantness surrounding this year's World Cup it's easy to forget that there's anything about it that can elicit a smile. But the story of Bosnia-Herzegovina captain Edin Dzeko sure can.

articles.title: War in Ukraine: Kyiv strikes key Russian supply lines
articles.description: Russian troops rely on supplies via the land corridor to Crimea, but Ukrainian forces are now able to launch concentrated attacks along the critical route. Experts say this indicates growing Russian vulnerability.

articles.title: The climate conversation many US pastors avoid
articles.description: As the Trump administration undoes scores of environmental protections, some Christian leaders are inviting their congregations to do as the Bible asks and be good stewards of the land. But many others stay silent.

articles.title: NASA picks first European astronaut for Artemis mission
articles.description: Italian astronaut Luca Parmitano will be the lead pilot for the Artemis III test flight. The NASA mission is expected to launch in 2027 to test technology for a future moon landing.

articles.title: Leipzig Bachfest 2026: Bach's music as hit parade
articles.description: The Leipzig Bach Festival honors the composer with a hit parade. Over 8,000 fans from 20 countries cast their votes. But Bach is celebrated in many other countries around the world as well.

articles.title: Germany upbeat as final World Cup preparations begin
articles.description: As the German men's national football team embark on their final preparations for the World Cup at their base camp in North Carolina, they're looking to make amends for disappointing tournaments in Russia and Qatar.

articles.title: Why Anthropic has the edge over OpenAI in IPO race
articles.description: The rivalry between Sam Altman and Dario Amodei is entering a new phase. Both AI bosses are planning public listings and hope to use the money to outpace each other in the race to build superintelligent AI.

articles.title: Will Ebola have an impact on the World Cup?
articles.description: While ticket prices, heat and politics have made headlines, Ebola has been a World Cup worry for DR Congo. The African nation has qualified for the first time in 52 years, but does the outbreak have wider implications?

articles.title: Somali referee denied US entry, dropped from FIFA World Cup 2026
articles.description: Omar Artan, Africa's top referee in 2025, was set to become the first Somali national to officiate at a FIFA World Cup before being denied entry by US authorities

articles.title: Will Mexico's World Cup party be spoiled by teacher protest?
articles.description: Just before the World Cup kicks off, host country Mexico faces a political tug-of-war. Striking teachers have occupied the central fan zone and have pledged to continue protesting.

articles.title: Depression in romantic relationships: You, me and the illness
articles.description: Depression can be a huge challenge for a relationship. Loved ones of someone with depression often feel helpless. But there is actually a lot they can do ― and a lot they shouldn't.

articles.title: Why the 2026 World Cup is so controversial
articles.description: The 2026 World Cup has come under fire even before kickoff. Criticism is mounting over US President Donald Trump’s travel bans, high ticket prices, the expansion to 48 teams as well as its environmental impact.

articles.title: Germany beat USA before World Cup but injuries cast shadow
articles.description: Germany’s final match before their World Cup start ended with a 2-1 win. But a tournament-ending injury to rising star Lennart Karl and doubts about veteran Manuel Neuer mean coach Julian Nagelsmann has work to do.

articles.title: High-functioning depression: When success masks suffering
articles.description: People with depression don't always feel overwhelmed or struggle to get things done — some are highly efficient and productive, despite their low moods. So it can't be that bad, right? Wrong!

articles.title: Why businesses are offering 'Quiet Hour'
articles.description: More peace and quiet, less stress — the Quiet Hour is an initiative for people with invisible disabilities. An increasing number of stores and institutions in Germany are launching similar campaigns.

articles.title: Desalination hopes and reformed poachers
articles.description: EVs surge in Ethiopia, former poachers offer seahorse tours and India's ghost villages are repopulated.

articles.title: SSRI antidepressants are often 'carelessly prescribed'
articles.description: SSRIs, like Prozac and Zoloft, are among the world's most-prescribed psychiatric drugs. These antidepressants help a lot of people. But they don't always work. In fact, some experts suggest they are overprescribed.

articles.title: Why Yad Vashem is coming to Germany
articles.description: "Remember" — every child in Israel knows the meaning of this Jewish commandment: Never forget the Holocaust. Now Yad Vashem wants to make sure people in Germany remember it too.

articles.description: Actress Nastassja Kinski spent years calling for the removal of a sexualized scene from Wim Wenders' film "The Wrong Move," in which she appeared topless at the age of 13.

articles.title: Google mosquito army: Scientists say 'we must take action'
articles.description: Google's Debug research program plans to release millions of sterile mosquitoes to fight species that spread diseases like dengue. How does the method work — and should humans interfere with nature like this?

articles.title: Saudi Arabia and Russia draw closer amid OPEC upheaval
articles.description: As Saudi Arabia and Russia deepen cooperation, their combined influence over global oil supply is growing. Could this shift the balance of power in energy markets?

articles.description: A low-budget horror film directed by a 20-year-old YouTuber is beating the new Star Wars movie at the box office. Behind its success is an entire viral online maze.

articles.title: Who owns the billions in Germany's dormant bank accounts?
articles.description: Billions of euros sit untouched in dormant bank accounts in Germany. With heirs unaware and no central register in place, banks and politicians are debating who should ultimately control the money.

articles.title: Legendary warrior women: The history of the Amazons
articles.description: They're said to have cut off their breasts to better draw their bows and even to have killed their male offspring. What is the history behind the myths surrounding the Amazons?

articles.title: Ethiopia goes electric following gas car ban
articles.description: Electric vehicles have taken off in Ethiopia. Key to the shift: a world-first ban on importing fossil fuel-powered vehicles.

articles.title: Mozart the idol: Searching for beauty in times of crisis
articles.description: Mozart's music evokes lightness and beauty. In times of war and destruction, people often invoke the ideals of the classical era. But is this just an escape from reality? The Mozartfest Würzburg offers different answers.

articles.title: How China keeps North Korea's economy alive
articles.description: Xi Jinping is visiting North Korea for the first time since 2019. Pyongyang relies on China for 95% of its legitimate trade; hacking, arms deals and remittances also help it stay afloat.

articles.title: German town prints its own cash to cut CO2 emissions
articles.description: It started as a school project to promote local businesses in a remote Bavarian region. Now, the "Chiemgauer" currency helps to cut emissions.

articles.title: DNA had one rule. Bacteria didn't get the memo
articles.description: Every cell in every organism on Earth copies DNA the same way. Except one bacterial protein — quietly doing something scientists had never seen before.

articles.title: Space race: Why Portugal is reaching for the stars
articles.description: A spaceport is being built on a small Portuguese island in the Atlantic. Is Portugal on the verge of becoming a space nation?

articles.title: Swing Youth: In Nazi Germany, jazz was an act of defiance
articles.description: The Nazis denounced jazz music as "degenerate art," despite its widespread popularity in Germany. As the Nazis clamped down on expression, groups of jazz-loving teenagers formed the Swing Youth to rebel.

articles.title: Goodbye, Norma Jeane: How Marilyn Monroe changed Hollywood
articles.description: Long seen primarily as a sex symbol, Marilyn Monroe is now viewed as an early advocate for women in Hollywood. On the 100th anniversary of her birth, DW looks at the star who balanced fame and feminist agency.

articles.title: Film funding bill to support blockbusters made in Germany
articles.description: The German government wants to attract more filmmakers and make the country a "global player" in on-screen entertainment. A new bill would require media companies to make mandatory investments in the film industry.

articles.description: The scaling back of development aid has contributed to the inability to contain the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo. German organizations are calling for a major spending boost to help stop the spread.
